content.title: About
content.content: Baby carrots are small, tender root vegetables harvested before full maturity. They have a sweet flavor, crisp texture, and bright orange color thanks to their high beta‑carotene content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Baby carrots contain two‑to‑three times more sugar than mature carrots, making them sweeter.
Beta‑carotene in carrots is converted by the body into vitamin A, essential for vision.
Young carrots are often used in baby foods because they are softer and easier to digest.
In some countries baby carrots are served as a snack, sliced into thin sticks.
Carrots were among the first vegetables domesticated by humans over 5,000 years ago.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is a precursor of vitamin A, supporting eyesight, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Baby carrots are low in calories, making them an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: In addition to beta‑carotene, carrots contain vitamin C and other antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium in carrots helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to carrots, such as skin rash or itching.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of raw carrots can cause gas and discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Soil contaminants
items.content: If grown in polluted soil, carrots may contain heavy metals; purchase from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baby carrots can be eaten raw as sticks, added to salads, blended into smoothies, or used as garnish. They may also be lightly blanched to soften the texture while retaining crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store carrots in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a plastic container with a small amount of water. Properly stored, they stay fresh for up to 2 weeks. Remove any wilted pieces to extend shelf life.
